ety.text: Shortening or back-formation of Middle English mappemounde, mapemounde (“world map”), from Old French mapamonde, from Medieval Latin mappa mundī, compound of Latin mappa (“napkin, cloth”) and mundus (“world”). See mop for more on the first component. Doublet of mop, nape, and nappe.

senses.d: A visual representation of an area, whether real or imaginary, showing the relative positions of places and other features.
ex: a map of Australia, a map of Lilliput
He bought a map for the tour of Edinburgh Castle.

senses.d: A graphical or logical representation of any structure or system, showing the positions of or relationships between its components.
ex: a map of the Earth's magnetic field
The 256 bytes of internal RAM are subdivided as shown in the memory map above.

senses.d: A function, especially a function satisfying a certain property (e.g. continuity, linearity, etc.; see Usage notes).
ex: Let f be a map from ℝ to ℝ

senses.d: Any of various nymphalid butterflies of the genera Araschnia (especially, Araschnia levana) and Cyrestis, having map-like markings on the wings.
The face.
An imaginary or fictional area, often predefined and confined, where a game or a session thereof takes place.
ex: I don't want to play this map again!
Jack loves playing on this Fortnite map.

senses.d: Synonym of associative array.
To represent by means of a map.
ex: This large atlas maps the whole world in very great detail.
Figure 3 maps the pressure distribution within the human circulatory system.

senses.d: To create a map of; to examine or survey in order to gather information for a map.
ex: The team is mapping the route of the new railway line.
The space probe is mapping the Earth's gravitational field.

senses.d: To have a direct relationship; to correspond.
ex: This doesn't map to my understanding of how things should work.
Significantly, the aural-oral data does not map closely to the visual linguistic landscape at NIE.

senses.d: To create a direct relationship to; to create a correspondence with.
ex: Map "volume down" to the F2 key.

senses.d: To act as a function on something, taking it to something else.
ex: f maps A to B, mapping every a∈A to f(a)∈B.
Equivalently: f:A→B,a↦f(a)

senses.d: To assign a drive letter to a shared folder.

ety.text: The noun is derived from Middle English mapel (“tree of species Acer campestre, sole native maple of the British Isles); wood of such a tree; artistic representation of a maple leaf; a beam, pole, stake (?)”), from Old English *mapul (attested in mapulder (“maple tree”), mapultrēow (“maple tree”), etc.), from Proto-West Germanic *mapul (“maple tree”), from Proto-Germanic *mapulaz; further etymology uncertain, possibly from *masuraz (“type of wood with spots or veins, such as maple or walnut”) (ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *mos- (“skin sore”)) + *aplaz (“apple; fruit”) (ultimately from P…
A variant of mapau, influenced by maple (etymology 1).

senses.d: Any member of any species of genus Acer, characterized by (usually) palmate, five-lobed leaves and winged seeds, and often grown for syrup or wood
ex: Russian maple
They have a large maple in their yard.

senses.d: A small tree (Acer campestre), known as the common maple, field maple, or hedge maple, which has palmate leaves with five lobes and winged seeds, and is chiefly native to East Asia, Europe, North Africa, and North America.

Often preceded by a descriptive word: a tree of the genus Acer; especially the sugar maple (Acer saccharum) native to North America which has brightly colored autumn foliage and is the primary source of maple syrup.
Chiefly preceded by a descriptive word: a tree of a genus other than Acer which has an appearance or wood similar to an Acer tree.
ex: Queensland maple

senses.d: Wood of an Acer tree, valued for its attractive appearance and hardness; also, similar wood from a tree of a genus other than Acer; (countable) a particular type of such wood.
ex: This table is made of maple and also has some fruitwood inlays.

senses.d: The light-brown color of the wood of a maple tree (etymology 1, noun sense 3).
The flavor of maple syrup made from the sap of a maple tree, or an imitation of that flavor.
ex: What flavour is your ice-cream? Mine’s maple—it’s delicious.

senses.d: Of the light-brown colour of the wood of a maple tree (etymology 1, noun sense 3).
Of the flavour of, or made with, maple syrup.
Synonym of mapau (“any of several trees of New Zealand, especially in the genus Myrsine”).
